name: Spring Boot
summary: A JVM application framework that prepares an environment, creates and refreshes a Spring application context, selects conditional auto-configuration, and can attach an embedded web server to that context.

features.name: Application-context startup orchestration
features.description: SpringApplication sequences environment preparation, application-context creation, context preparation and loading, context refresh, startup listeners, runners, and failure handling.
benefits: Exposes listener and initializer extension points
costs: Startup spans several callback and context phases
Refresh failures can cross bean and environment interactions

features.name: Conditional auto-configuration
features.description: Spring Boot discovers auto-configuration candidates and filters them according to metadata and conditions so the application context receives conventional infrastructure when relevant classes, beans, and properties are present.
benefits: Reduces explicit configuration for common deployments
Lets classpath and environment select infrastructure
costs: Effective configuration depends on classpath, conditions, properties, and ordering
Unexpected condition outcomes can be difficult to inspect

features.name: Environment, profile, and property model
features.description: SpringApplication creates and configures an Environment with property sources and profiles, binds application properties, and passes that environment into context configuration.
costs: Property precedence and profiles add state
Runtime behavior varies with environment inputs

features.name: Embedded web-server application context
features.description: For servlet web applications, Spring Boot uses a web-capable application context that can create and start an embedded web server and publish the server namespace through the context lifecycle.
benefits: Packages application and web-server startup together
Lets web infrastructure participate in context refresh
costs: Server availability is coupled to context refresh
Embedded deployment differs from external-container assumptions

mathematical_views.question: How does a process move from argument and environment preparation to a refreshed, running application context?
assumptions: Environment preparation, context creation, loading, refresh, and readiness are ordered transitions
Failure transitions may close a partial context

mathematical_views.question: Which configuration candidates and beans become part of the context under a given classpath, property, and bean environment?
assumptions: Configuration classes and beans are vertices with imports and condition guards
Condition evaluation selects a candidate subgraph
Selection does not prove semantic compatibility

mathematical_views.question: How do profiles and property sources select a different application configuration while retaining one codebase?
assumptions: An environment is a tuple of property sources, profiles, and arguments
Context configuration is a partial function from that tuple to a bean graph
Precedence and external secret management are abstracted

benefits: A shared lifecycle supports diverse JVM entry points
costs: Failures can cross environment, context, bean, listener, and runner phases

benefits: Conventionally useful infrastructure needs less explicit configuration
costs: Classpath and condition state make effective configuration less explicit

benefits: One artifact can serve multiple environments
costs: Precedence and profile combinations enlarge runtime configuration space

benefits: Web server and context deploy together
costs: Readiness and server lifecycle couple to context refresh
